exercises.Name: Abdominal Brace
Howto: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Gently tighten your abdominal muscles as if bracing for a light poke, without holding your breath.
Keep your lower back neutral — don't let it arch up or flatten hard into the floor.
Hold, breathing normally, then relax.
exercises.Mistakes: Letting the lower back arch off the floor; holding the breath instead of breathing normally.

Sources.Title: AAOS OrthoInfo — Spine Conditioning Program

Levels.Notes: Extend one leg at a time — the lowest-load version.

Levels.Label: L2 — Opposite arm + leg
Levels.Notes: Hold 15 s, daily (AAOS). Plymouth doses this as 15 alternating reps, 5 s hold each.

exercises.Name: Side Plank (Knees)
Howto: Lie on your side with your knees bent and stacked, propped up on your forearm.
Lift your hips off the floor until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Hold the position, then lower with control.
Repeat on the other side.

Sources.Title: AAOS OrthoInfo — Spine Conditioning Program

exercises.Name: Side Plank

Levels.Label: From feet
Levels.Notes: No verified dose — set by your physiotherapist. Progress from Side Plank (Knees) only once that's pain-free.

exercises.Cautions: Only after the knees version is pain-free.

exercises.Name: Partial Curl Up
Howto: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hands resting lightly behind your head or crossed on your chest.
Curl your head and shoulders a few inches off the floor, keeping your lower back pressed down.
Hold briefly, then lower with control.
exercises.Cautions: Flexion-direction exercise — check this matches your physiotherapist's preferred direction.

exercises.Name: Glute Bridge

Levels.Label: Standard (AAOS)
Levels.Notes: Hold 15 s, daily. Plymouth doses this as 15 reps with no hold.

exercises.Mistakes: Arching the lower back (Plymouth) — keep it neutral.

Sources.Title: AAOS OrthoInfo — Spine Conditioning Program

exercises.Name: Pelvic Tilt
Howto: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Slowly flatten your lower back into the floor by gently tilting your pelvis, then release into a slight arch.
Move slowly between the two positions, staying within a pain-free range.

Sources.Title: Cambridge University Hospitals — Back mobility exercises
Plymouth Hospitals NHS — Back rehabilitation programme

exercises.Name: Knee to Chest Stretch
Howto: Lie on your back with both knees bent.
Bring one knee toward your chest, holding behind the thigh.
Hold gently, then lower and repeat on the other side.

Levels.Label: Standard (AAOS)
Levels.Notes: 5 s hold per rep. Plymouth doses this as 5–10 reps, 15 s hold, per leg.

exercises.Cautions: Flexion-direction exercise — check this matches your physiotherapist's preferred direction.

Sources.Title: AAOS OrthoInfo — Spine Conditioning Program
Cambridge University Hospitals — Back mobility exercises

exercises.Name: Bottom to Heel Stretch
Howto: Kneel on all fours, then sit your hips back toward your heels.
Let your arms stretch forward and your back round gently.
Hold for one breath, then return to the starting position.
exercises.Cautions: Flexion-direction exercise — check this matches your physiotherapist's preferred direction.

Sources.Title: Plymouth Hospitals NHS — Back rehabilitation programme

exercises.Name: Knee Rolls
Howto: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor, arms out to the sides.
Slowly let both knees fall to one side, keeping both shoulders on the floor.
Return to the centre and repeat on the other side.
exercises.Mistakes: Shoulders lifting off the floor; letting the upper trunk move (keep it in the pelvis).

Sources.Title: Cambridge University Hospitals — Back mobility exercises
Plymouth Hospitals NHS — Back rehabilitation programme

exercises.Name: Cat Camel
Howto: Start on all fours, hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Slowly round your back toward the ceiling, then let it sag gently into a slight arch.
Move slowly and smoothly between the two positions.

Levels.Label: Standard
Levels.Notes: 8–10 reps. Moves through both flexion and extension, so it isn't tagged to either.

Sources.Title: Plymouth Hospitals NHS — Back rehabilitation programme

exercises.Name: Prone Press Up
Howto: Lie face down, propped up on your forearms (or hands, for the straight-arm version).
Let your lower back relax and sink gently, keeping your hips and legs on the floor.
Hold, then lower back down with control.

Levels.Label: L1 — On forearms
Levels.Notes: 8–10 reps, 5–10 s hold each (Plymouth). CUH leaves the exact dose for your physiotherapist to set.

Levels.Label: L2 — Arms straight
Levels.Notes: Progress here once L1 is comfortable.

exercises.Mistakes: Tensing the hips or legs — keep your pelvis and legs relaxed.
exercises.Cautions: Extension-direction exercise — check this matches your physiotherapist's preferred direction.
